questions.question: What is Base?
options: An Ethereum Layer 2 built on the OP Stack
questions.explanation: Base is an Ethereum Layer 2 (optimistic rollup) built on the Optimism OP Stack, incubated by Coinbase.

questions.question: Who incubated Base?
questions.explanation: Base was incubated by Coinbase and is part of the Optimism Superchain.

questions.question: What is Base's mainnet chain ID?
questions.explanation: Base Mainnet uses chain ID 8453. Base Sepolia testnet uses 84532.

questions.question: What is Base Sepolia's chain ID?
questions.explanation: Base Sepolia is the test network with chain ID 84532. Sepolia (Ethereum L1 testnet) is 11155111.

questions.question: Which native token pays for gas on Base?
questions.explanation: Like most Ethereum L2s, Base uses ETH as the native gas token. There is no token called BASE.

questions.question: What is Base's block time approximately?
questions.explanation: Base produces blocks every ~2 seconds, which is faster than Ethereum L1's 12s slot time.

questions.question: Which underlying technology stack does Base use?
questions.explanation: Base is built on the Optimism OP Stack and is part of the Optimism Superchain.

questions.question: What is the role of Base's sequencer?
options: Validates ZK proofs of state transitions
Orders incoming transactions and produces L2 blocks
Hosts the public RPC endpoint only
questions.explanation: The sequencer accepts user transactions, orders them, and produces L2 blocks; data is later posted to L1 for settlement.

questions.question: Where does Base post data for L1 settlement?
questions.explanation: Base posts batched transaction data to Ethereum mainnet (calldata historically; blobs since EIP-4844) to inherit Ethereum's security.

questions.question: Which type of rollup is Base?
questions.explanation: Base is an optimistic rollup using fault proofs to challenge invalid state transitions.

questions.question: What is the official block explorer for Base?
questions.explanation: BaseScan (basescan.org) is Etherscan's branded explorer for Base. The Etherscan team operates it.

questions.question: Which hardfork introduced a configurable minimum base fee on Base?
questions.explanation: The Jovian hardfork introduced a configurable minimum base fee via SystemConfig and a DA footprint gas scalar.

questions.question: Which predeploy contract on Base exposes L1 attributes (block number, basefee) to L2 contracts?
questions.explanation: The L1Block predeploy exposes the latest known L1 block attributes to L2 smart contracts.

questions.question: Are smart contracts on Base written in the same language as Ethereum L1?
options: Yes, but only a Base-specific dialect of Solidity
questions.explanation: Base is EVM-equivalent: any Solidity or Vyper contract that compiles for EVM works on Base unchanged.

questions.question: What is the typical canonical bridge withdrawal time from Base to Ethereum L1?
questions.explanation: Native canonical withdrawals require the ~7-day challenge period typical of optimistic rollups. Third-party fast bridges shortcut this with liquidity.

questions.question: What is the Optimism Superchain?
options: A staking pool that secures all OP chains
A shared standard and interop layer for OP-Stack-based chains
A separate L1 chain by Optimism
Optimism's marketing term for sequencer redundancy
questions.explanation: The Superchain is a shared standard and interop framework that lets multiple OP-Stack chains (Base, Optimism, Mode, etc.) share security and tooling.

questions.question: What is the canonical mainnet RPC endpoint provided by Base?
questions.explanation: https://mainnet.base.org is the canonical public endpoint; https://sepolia.base.org is the testnet equivalent.

questions.question: What does the Pectra Blob Schedule hardfork on Base concern?
options: Adoption schedule for Ethereum's increased blob count
Switch from optimistic to ZK proofs
questions.explanation: The Pectra Blob Schedule is an optional hardfork that delays Base's adoption of Ethereum's increased blob count schedule.

questions.question: Roughly what does a simple ETH transfer typically cost on Base mainnet?
options: Cents to fractions of a cent
questions.explanation: Base targets fractions of a cent to a few cents per simple transaction, depending on L1 blob price and demand.

questions.question: What did Base introduce on September 10, 2025?
options: A switch from ETH to USDC for gas
A per-transaction maximum gas cap enforced by the chain
questions.explanation: On September 10, 2025 Base began enforcing a per-transaction gas cap to limit single-tx gas pressure on the network.

questions.question: What is Base Account?
options: An ERC-4337 smart contract wallet with universal sign-in
questions.explanation: Base Account is an ERC-4337 smart contract wallet that supports universal sign-in (passkeys), batch transactions, and one-tap USDC payments via Base Pay.

questions.question: Which authentication method is central to Base Account onboarding?
questions.explanation: Base Account uses passkeys for sign-in — biometric / OS-level credentials that remove the friction of seed phrases.

questions.question: Which EIP standardises sending a batch of calls in one wallet RPC request?
questions.explanation: EIP-5792 introduces wallet_sendCalls / wallet_getCallsStatus / wallet_getCapabilities for batch and capability-aware UX.

questions.question: What does the Spend Permissions capability enable?
options: Letting an app pre-authorize recurring USDC charges from the user
questions.explanation: Spend Permissions let users grant a scoped, revocable allowance — the basis for USDC subscriptions in Base Pay.

questions.question: What is a Base Account Sub Account?
options: A second seed phrase for the wallet
An app-scoped sub-wallet with its own permissions
A delegate signer that controls the main wallet
questions.explanation: Sub Accounts are app-specific scoped accounts under the main Base Account, useful for isolating risk per dApp.

questions.question: What does the paymasterService capability do in Base Account?
options: Signs cheques for off-chain payment rails
Enables gas sponsorship for users via ERC-4337 paymaster web services
Refunds gas after a failed transaction
questions.explanation: paymasterService advertises ERC-4337 paymaster URLs so dApps can sponsor gas for end-users.

questions.question: What does the auxiliaryFunds capability indicate?
options: The wallet supports lending to other users
The wallet has access to funds beyond what is verifiable on-chain (e.g., custodial reserves)
The wallet was funded via a faucet
Funds are locked in a vault
questions.explanation: auxiliaryFunds tells dApps the wallet (e.g., Coinbase Wallet) can pull from off-chain balances if needed.

questions.question: Which RPC method queries a wallet's supported capabilities?
questions.explanation: wallet_getCapabilities returns the set of capabilities (atomicBatch, paymasterService, auxiliaryFunds, etc.) for a given account.

questions.question: Can a typical EOA (externally-owned account) submit batch transactions via EIP-5792?
options: Only when using a hardware wallet
No — only smart wallets can; dApps must detect and fall back
questions.explanation: EOAs cannot atomically batch — only smart wallets (e.g., Base Account) can. Apps should call wallet_getCapabilities and gracefully fall back to sequential writes.

questions.question: What is a Basename?
options: A human-readable identifier ending in .base for a Base Account
A Coinbase username separate from the wallet
questions.explanation: Basenames are human-readable .base identifiers tied to Base wallets — like ENS but native to Base.

questions.question: What is the recommended authentication pattern in the Base App after April 9, 2026?
options: Sign-In with Ethereum (SIWE) using wagmi useSignMessage
questions.explanation: After the migration to standard web app + wallet, apps use SIWE for authenticated sessions.

questions.question: Which RPC method submits a batch of calls to the wallet for execution?
questions.explanation: wallet_sendCalls is the EIP-5792 method used to atomically submit multiple calls.

questions.question: What does dataCallback capability allow a Base Account to do during a transaction?
options: Replay the transaction in the future
Collect personal information (email, address, phone, name) from the user
questions.explanation: dataCallback is a Base Account capability that lets dApps request user information (email, shipping address, etc.) inline with a transaction.

questions.question: Which RPC method returns the status of a previously submitted batch?
questions.explanation: wallet_getCallsStatus is the EIP-5792 query for the status (pending / confirmed / failed) of a submitted batch.

questions.question: Why is checking wallet_getCapabilities important before attempting a batch?
options: To prevent the user from being charged twice
Because EOAs don't support batching, so apps must fall back gracefully
Because batches need a special token
questions.explanation: Capabilities querying lets apps detect smart-wallet features (atomicBatch, paymasterService) and gracefully fall back to sequential transactions for EOAs.

questions.question: What is the Base App?
options: Coinbase's social and wallet super-app where Mini Apps live
questions.explanation: Base App is Coinbase's social/wallet super-app that hosts Mini Apps — small web apps with wallet access.

questions.question: Starting April 9, 2026, what model does the Base App use for Mini Apps?
options: Standard web app + wallet (registered on base.dev)
questions.explanation: After April 9, 2026, the Base App treats all apps as standard web apps with an injected wallet, and discovery is powered by base.dev metadata.

questions.question: What is base.dev in the Mini Apps ecosystem?
options: The project registry, metadata host, and dev preview tool for Mini Apps
questions.explanation: base.dev is where developers register projects, configure metadata, get builder codes, preview embeds, and access Builder Rewards info.

questions.question: What is MiniKit?
options: A CLI for deploying smart contracts
A React SDK for building Mini Apps with wagmi/react-query/Farcaster connector preconfigured
questions.explanation: MiniKit is the React-based SDK that wires up wagmi, react-query, and connector context for Mini Apps.

questions.question: Which MiniKit hook initializes the Mini App context (user info, host)?
questions.explanation: useMiniKit returns context (user, client) and exposes setFrameReady() that the app must call once on first render.

questions.question: How should a Mini App open external URLs to keep users in-app?
options: Use the useOpenUrl hook from MiniKit
questions.explanation: Raw links risk breaking out of the host. useOpenUrl uses the host's native browser flow.

questions.question: What field in the manifest powers Mini App discovery / categorisation?
questions.explanation: primaryCategory (e.g., "social", "defi", "games") drives where the app appears in search and category views.

questions.question: What does noindex: true in a Mini App manifest do?
options: Hides the app from Base.dev search while testing
Makes the app invisible to all users
questions.explanation: noindex prevents indexing during pre-launch testing so half-baked apps don't surface in discovery.

questions.question: What is a Builder Code?
options: An identifier that attributes app activity / volume to a specific builder for rewards
questions.explanation: Builder Codes attach attribution to onchain activity originating from a Mini App, powering Builder Rewards distribution.

questions.question: Which Farcaster SDK method's deeplink replacement is used to view a wallet profile in Base App?
questions.explanation: viewProfile is replaced by the deeplink https://base.app/profile/WALLET_ADDRESS.

questions.question: Which Farcaster SDK method has NO replacement in the post-April-2026 Base App?
questions.explanation: requestCameraAndMicrophoneAccess (and close, viewCast, composeCast) have no replacement — apps fall back to standard web APIs or omit the feature.

questions.question: What's the recommended onboarding behavior for a Mini App on first render?
options: Show a Connect Wallet button immediately
Show value instantly with one clear CTA; defer auth/wallet prompts until needed
questions.explanation: Frictionless onboarding is the official guidance: deliver value immediately, prompt for auth only when truly required.

questions.question: What's the role of the embed image in a Mini App post?
options: It's the preview that converts feed impressions into app launches
questions.explanation: Compelling embed images plus a clear launch CTA are the primary lever for turning impressions into launches in feeds.

questions.question: Which file path holds the manifest for a Farcaster-style Mini App pre-migration?
questions.explanation: Farcaster Mini App manifests historically lived at /.well-known/farcaster.json. Post-migration, metadata is hosted on base.dev.

questions.question: What is the simplest in-product way to publish a registered Mini App?
options: Submit a PR to the Base monorepo
Create a post in the Base App with the app's URL
Mint an NFT representing the app
questions.explanation: After registering on base.dev, you publish by creating a post in the Base App that contains your app's URL — the embed renders automatically.

questions.question: What is OnchainKit?
options: A React component library and toolkit for building polished onchain UX
questions.explanation: OnchainKit is Coinbase's React component library covering wallet connect, identity, swaps, transactions, NFTs, and more.

questions.question: Which OnchainKit React component renders a connect-wallet button + state?
questions.explanation: OnchainKit's <Wallet /> component encapsulates the connect, address display, and dropdown menu.

questions.question: What does the OnchainKit <Identity /> component show?
options: Avatar, basename / ENS, address — branded user identity
questions.explanation: <Identity /> displays a user's avatar, basename (or ENS), and shortened address consistently across the app.

questions.question: Which OnchainKit component wraps a write transaction and surfaces pending / success / error states?
questions.explanation: <Transaction /> handles the entire flow: build, simulate, broadcast, confirm — surfacing each state to the user.

questions.question: Why does OnchainKitProvider take an apiKey prop?
options: To unlock Coinbase developer APIs (price, indexer, identity resolution, etc.)
It's a payment for using the library
To bypass rate limits on Etherscan
questions.explanation: The API key authorizes server-side calls to Coinbase developer services used by OnchainKit components.

questions.question: Which providers does OnchainKitProvider configure under the hood?
questions.explanation: OnchainKitProvider sets up wagmi + react-query and exposes shared context — saving you boilerplate.

questions.question: What does the <Swap /> component do?
options: Lets users swap tokens via routed liquidity (Coinbase routing infra)
questions.explanation: <Swap /> is a drop-in token-swap UI that handles quotes, allowances, and execution via Coinbase routing.

questions.question: Which component pair is used to mint and showcase NFTs?
questions.explanation: OnchainKit ships <NFTMint /> for the mint flow and <NFTCard /> for displaying NFTs.

questions.question: Where does the OnchainKit Wallet component fit relative to MiniKit?
options: MiniKitProvider wraps OnchainKit context — they're complementary
questions.explanation: MiniKitProvider wraps and configures OnchainKitProvider, so the two work together with no extra setup.

questions.question: Which framework do most OnchainKit and MiniKit examples assume?
questions.explanation: Examples and quickstarts use Next.js with the App Router — though any React-based stack works.

questions.question: What is USDC?
options: A US-dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Circle
questions.explanation: USDC is the regulated US-dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Circle. It's natively issued on Base.

questions.question: Which is the canonical native USDC contract on Base mainnet?
questions.explanation: 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 is native USDC on Base; the others are USDT or other-chain addresses.

questions.question: How many decimals does USDC use?
questions.explanation: USDC uses 6 decimals — common bug source if devs assume 18-decimal scaling.

questions.question: What does Base Pay enable?
options: One-tap USDC payments and recurring USDC subscriptions via smart wallets
questions.explanation: Base Pay turns Base Account + Spend Permissions into a one-tap USDC payment + subscription primitive for apps.

questions.question: What is x402?
options: An HTTP-native payment protocol where APIs charge per-request via crypto
A new HTTP status code for missing pages
questions.explanation: x402 is an HTTP payment protocol that lets services charge per request — agents (and humans) can pay micro-amounts to access APIs.

questions.question: Which Base Pay function executes a recurring USDC charge from the backend?
questions.explanation: subscription.charge runs a charge against a previously-granted Spend Permission via a CDP server wallet.

questions.question: What's the difference between USDC and USDbC on Base?
options: USDC is bridged from Ethereum, USDbC is native
USDbC is bridged (legacy); USDC is natively issued by Circle and preferred
They're identical, just different brand names
USDbC is for businesses, USDC for retail
questions.explanation: USDbC was the older bridged USDC. Once Circle launched native USDC on Base, projects migrated; USDbC is considered legacy.

questions.question: Which method retrieves the status of a Base Pay payment?
questions.explanation: getPaymentStatus returns the lifecycle state of a payment transaction in Base Pay.

questions.question: How is a subscription cancelled / revoked from the backend?
questions.explanation: subscription.revoke removes the underlying Spend Permission so no further charges can be made.

questions.question: What is subscription.getOrCreateSubscriptionOwnerWallet?
options: A function that mints a new ERC-20
A method that returns or creates a CDP smart wallet to act as the subscription owner
questions.explanation: It provisions a CDP-backed smart wallet that owns the Spend Permission and is the address from which charges are settled.

questions.question: Which AMM/DEX is the largest by liquidity on Base and uses a ve(3,3) model?
questions.explanation: Aerodrome (a Velodrome fork) is Base's largest DEX, using the ve(3,3) tokenomics model.

questions.question: What category does Morpho on Base fit into?
questions.explanation: Morpho is a lending protocol on Base (and other EVM chains) optimized for capital efficiency.

questions.question: What is the canonical bridge for Base?
questions.explanation: bridge.base.org is the official native bridge using the OP Stack canonical-bridge contracts.

questions.question: What's the main UX difference between the canonical bridge and a third-party bridge (Across, Stargate)?
options: Canonical takes ~7 days for L2→L1; third parties give instant liquidity for a fee
Third parties are riskier and never used
questions.explanation: Canonical L2→L1 withdrawals must wait the challenge period; third-party bridges front liquidity for a small fee.

questions.question: What does Uniswap V4's hooks feature enable?
options: Custom logic at pool lifecycle events (initialise, swap, modifyLiquidity, donate)
questions.explanation: Hooks let pool creators inject custom logic at pool events, enabling things like dynamic fees, TWAMM, on-chain limit orders.

questions.question: What does an LP (liquidity provider) contribute to a DEX?
options: Pairs of tokens (or single-sided in some designs) used to fill swaps, in exchange for trading fees
questions.explanation: LPs deposit token pairs into pools and earn a share of trading fees proportional to their liquidity.

questions.question: What does TVL stand for?
questions.explanation: TVL = Total Value Locked, a common metric for the assets deposited in a protocol.

questions.question: What is impermanent loss?
options: A bug that locks LP tokens
The opportunity cost an LP suffers when pool token prices diverge vs. simply holding the tokens
questions.explanation: Impermanent loss is the gap between LP value and just-holding-the-tokens; it crystallises when an LP withdraws.

questions.question: Which lending protocol focuses on single-asset, borrow-only markets and exists on Base?
questions.explanation: Compound III (Comet) markets have a single borrowable asset with multiple collateral types and isolated risk.

questions.question: What is concentrated liquidity (Uniswap V3 / V4 model)?
options: Liquidity providers choose a price range to provide liquidity within, achieving higher capital efficiency
Pooling all DEX liquidity into one pool
questions.explanation: Concentrated liquidity lets LPs concentrate capital into specific price ranges — higher efficiency, but higher impermanent loss risk if price exits range.

questions.question: What is Farcaster?
options: A decentralised social protocol with public posts (casts) and channels
questions.explanation: Farcaster is a decentralised social protocol; Warpcast and other clients render the Farcaster network.

questions.question: What does FID stand for in Farcaster?
questions.explanation: FID = Farcaster ID, a numeric identifier for users on the Farcaster network.

questions.question: What is a 'cast' in Farcaster terminology?
questions.explanation: A cast is a public Farcaster post (analogous to a tweet).

questions.question: What's a Farcaster channel?
options: A topic-based community where casts are aggregated
A bridge between Farcaster and X (Twitter)
questions.explanation: Channels are topic-based communities — like subreddits on top of the Farcaster graph.

questions.question: What is the relationship between Frames and Mini Apps in 2026?
options: Frames are the new name for Mini Apps
Mini Apps replaced Frames v2 in the Base App with a standard-web-app + wallet model
questions.explanation: Mini Apps evolved out of Frames, and after April 9, 2026 the Base App treats them as standard web apps with an injected wallet.

questions.question: Pre-migration, what role did Neynar play for Mini Apps?
options: Hosted Farcaster hubs and webhook infrastructure (FID-based notifications)
questions.explanation: Neynar provided hosted Farcaster hubs, APIs, and webhooks (e.g., add/remove events, notifications) for Mini App developers.

questions.question: After April 9, 2026, what addressing scheme does the Base.dev notifications API use?
questions.explanation: Base.dev notifications target users by wallet address (replacing FID-based notifications via Neynar).

questions.question: Which Farcaster SDK action lets a Mini App open a cast composer prefilled with content?
questions.explanation: composeCast opened the cast composer with prefilled text/embeds. (It has no replacement in the Base App after migration — there's nothing equivalent needed.)

questions.question: What is Warpcast?
options: A popular Farcaster client (and the original one) by Merkle Manufactory
questions.explanation: Warpcast is the leading Farcaster client built by Merkle Manufactory.

questions.question: What is one strong viral mechanic Mini Apps should design for, per the growth playbook?
options: Native share-to-cast flows that turn single-player moments into threads / returns
questions.explanation: Native share / social-graph integration converts single-user actions into threaded conversations and re-acquisition.

questions.question: Which is the standard Etherscan-style explorer for Base?
questions.explanation: BaseScan (basescan.org) is the canonical block explorer for Base, run by the Etherscan team.

questions.question: Which company runs the Ethereum Attestation Service (EAS)?
options: Ethereum Attestation Service is a public good, not run by a single company
questions.explanation: EAS is an open public good — anyone can register schemas and create attestations on supported chains, including Base.

questions.question: What is an EAS Schema?
options: A typed structure defining the data layout of attestations of a given kind
questions.explanation: Schemas in EAS define the typed fields of an attestation (e.g., 'address user, uint8 level'). They're registered once via the Schema Registry.

questions.question: What is a typical use case for an EAS attestation?
options: Creating a verifiable signed claim about an address (e.g., "is KYC-verified", "holds level 5")
questions.explanation: EAS attestations are signed, on-chain (or hashed onchain) claims about an address — KYC, level, reputation, audit, etc.

questions.question: Which RPC providers are commonly used for Base mainnet besides the public endpoint?
questions.explanation: Standard EVM RPC providers operate on Base — Alchemy, QuickNode, Coinbase Cloud, Infura, etc. Tenderly is a debugger / simulator, not primarily an RPC.

questions.question: Which platform is widely used to simulate / debug transactions on Base?
questions.explanation: Tenderly provides simulation, debugger, and alerting for EVM chains including Base.

questions.question: Which is a popular subgraph / data indexing platform usable on Base?
questions.explanation: The Graph (and Goldsky, Envio) supports Base for declarative event indexing and queries.

questions.question: What's the safest pattern for app-side wallet capability detection?
options: Check capabilities against your deployment chain (not the wallet's current chain) before attempting batch
questions.explanation: useChainId returns the wallet's current chain, not your deployment chain — checking capabilities against the wrong chain is a known footgun.

questions.question: What are Builder Rewards on Base?
options: Tokens given to all users for signing in
Onchain rewards that go to active builders shipping useful apps on Base
questions.explanation: Builder Rewards are an onchain incentive program that distributes rewards to active builders, attributed via Builder Codes.

questions.question: When designing a Mini App, which of the following is NOT recommended by the launch checklist?
options: Show a Connect Wallet modal as the very first interaction
Use clear primary CTAs and respect mobile safe areas
questions.explanation: Forcing Connect-Wallet as the first interaction is explicitly anti-pattern in the onboarding guide. Defer wallet/auth prompts until value has been delivered.
